title: Dow Drops 700 Points as Tech Slumps; Traders Watch Reported NSA Network Outage – Live Updates.
body:
Wall Street slipped sharply on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average shedding more than 700 points as a wave of disappointing earnings and a sudden dip in technology stocks pulled the market lower. The decline came amid heightened anxiety over a reported outage at the National Security Agency’s (NSA) internal network, which traders feared could signal broader cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Investors also awaited Nvidia’s upcoming quarterly report, a key catalyst that could either buoy the tech‑heavy index or deepen the sell‑off.

The drop was led by a cluster of heavyweight tech names that opened lower after mixed results from recent earnings releases. Semiconductor maker Broadcom posted revenue that missed analysts’ expectations, while software firm ServiceNow warned of slower growth in its subscription base. The downward pressure was compounded by a sell‑off in the broader technology sector, with the Nasdaq Composite falling nearly 2 % as investors trimmed exposure to high‑growth stocks that have been driving market gains this year. By mid‑session, the Dow was down 708.12 points, or 2.1 %, closing the day near the 35,000‑point threshold that many had hoped to sustain.

Adding to the market’s unease was an unconfirmed report that the NSA experienced a temporary disruption to its internal communications network. While details remain scarce, the incident sparked speculation that the breach could be linked to a sophisticated cyber‑attack, raising concerns about the resilience of critical U.S. infrastructure. Analysts cautioned that even a brief outage at a key intelligence agency could have ripple effects across the technology sector, where many firms depend on government contracts and secure data handling. “When the nation’s own security apparatus shows signs of strain, it can quickly erode confidence in the broader tech ecosystem,” said Karen Liu, senior market strategist at Meridian Capital.

On the macro side, the European Union’s executive arm released an upbeat forecast, raising its growth projection for the bloc after an “upward surprise” in the first three quarters of the year. The revision was driven by a rebound in exports and robust consumer spending, especially in Germany and France. While the EU’s optimism provided a counterweight to the U.S. market’s turbulence, it did little to stem the immediate sell‑off. “European data is encouraging, but American investors are currently focused on domestic earnings and the looming cloud of a potential cyber‑security breach,” noted Michael O’Connor, chief economist at Global Insight.

Nvidia’s earnings, slated for later in the day, have become a focal point for market participants. The chipmaker’s latest results are expected to reveal whether demand for graphics processing units (GPUs) and artificial‑intelligence (AI) accelerators remains resilient amid a cooling macro environment. A strong performance could reignite optimism in the tech sector and help the Dow recover some of its losses, while a miss might deepen the correction and trigger further risk‑off trading. “Nvidia has been the poster child for AI‑driven growth; any sign of slowdown would be a red flag for investors who have been heavily weighted toward tech,” Liu added.

Looking ahead, analysts suggest that the market’s near‑term trajectory will hinge on a combination of corporate earnings, the resolution of the NSA network issue, and broader geopolitical developments. If the NSA outage proves to be an isolated incident, confidence could rebound quickly, especially if Nvidia delivers a beat‑and‑raise. Conversely, a prolonged investigation or additional cyber‑security scares could keep risk appetite muted, prompting investors to rotate into defensive sectors such as utilities and consumer staples. As the trading day closed, the Dow hovered near the 34,900‑point mark, underscoring the volatility that has become a hallmark of the current market cycle. Traders will be watching closely for any fresh data that could tip the balance between optimism and caution in the weeks to come.
